transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Ah, Maestro Salieri! A pleasure to see you, though I confess I did not expect to have the honour today. Please, come in, come in from the chill. How may I be of service to you this afternoon? I fear the Master is away on business, visiting suppliers in Pressburg and beyond, and will not return for several weeks. But I am here to assist with whatever I can.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, Signor Benda, for your hospitality. I understand that the Master is currently away. However, I have an urgent matter that requires his immediate attention. It concerns a custom fortepiano that was recently delivered to the Imperial Court's music room. There seems to be several issues with the instrument, including stuck keys, a faulty pedal mechanism, and a thin and tinny tone in the upper register. I require your assistance in rectifying these problems immediately. We cannot afford any delays, as the piano is meant to be used for upcoming concerts and performances.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Ah, I see. A matter concerning the new fortepiano, you say. That *is* a grave concern, naturally, and I appreciate your urgency, Maestro. The Master himself oversaw much of that particular commission, a true marvel of craftsmanship, if I may say so.

However, as I mentioned, the Master is quite far afield, and will not return for at least a month, perhaps more, given the state of the roads this season. And I must regretfully inform you that all commissions from this workshop are considered fulfilled upon delivery and acceptance. The Court’s own servants, if I recall correctly, signed the receipt just a few weeks ago, affirming their satisfaction. Our guild rules, Maestro, are quite strict on such matters; they explicitly forbid reopening a completed commission without the Master’s personal and direct approval. Without him here, I am, unfortunately, quite unable to act on your request for repairs or replacement. My hands are tied by regulation.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I understand your position, Signor Benda. Your loyalty to the guild rules is commendable. However, we are dealing with an exceptional situation here. The piano in question is of utmost importance for our musical endeavors, and we cannot afford to wait for the Master's return. Is there any possibility to obtain his approval through a written statement or some other means? Time is of the essence, and we need to ensure the piano is in proper working condition as soon as possible.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Maestro, I truly wish there were. Believe me, I understand the pressures of the Court, and your reputation precedes you. But the Master's approval for reopening a completed commission is not a matter for simple correspondence. These are decisions of significant import, often requiring his direct inspection, or at the very least, a detailed account from *him* to the guild.

He is not merely visiting Pressburg, you see; he is journeying further east, seeking out rare timbers and new suppliers, often in remote villages where even a reliable courier might struggle to reach, let alone return with a sealed reply in any timely fashion. Sending word, let alone receiving a legally binding instruction from him on such a sensitive matter, would take weeks, perhaps longer, even if we were to send a rider expressly for that purpose. And by then, the Master himself might well be on his way back.

My hands remain tied, I'm afraid. Without his personal presence and assessment, I am entirely unable to authorize any work on the instrument, much less a replacement. It would be a breach of guild law and a direct defiance of the Master's authority in his absence.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I appreciate your honesty, Signor Benda. It is unfortunate that we find ourselves in such a predicament. We must rely on the expertise of the instrument-maker and seek alternative solutions. Perhaps we can explore the possibility of modifying the piano to address the specific issues we have encountered. We cannot let this setback deter us from our musical pursuits. We must find a way to ensure the piano is in optimal condition for our upcoming concerts and performances. Thank you for your understanding and cooperation in this matter. I will consult with the instrument-maker and explore alternative courses of action.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Maestro Salieri, I understand completely your drive to ensure the highest quality for your performances. Music, after all, demands nothing less.

However, any modifications to an instrument built by our workshop, particularly one of such recent and prominent commission, would fall under the same strictures as repairs or replacements. Without the Master's explicit instruction and approval, I cannot permit any alterations by *our* hands. And if you seek to have another craftsperson modify it, that would, of course, be entirely outside of our purview and responsibility.

I truly regret that I cannot offer you the direct assistance you seek within the framework of our workshop's regulations and the Master's absence. I wish you the very best in finding a swift resolution for the Court's musical needs.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, Signor Benda, for your understanding and adherence to the rules. I appreciate your dedication to the standards and traditions of our craft. Rest assured, we will explore alternative solutions to ensure the piano meets our expectations. We cannot let this setback hinder our musical aspirations. We shall rely on the expertise of the instrument-maker and find a suitable resolution. Thank you again for your time and assistance. I wish you the best of luck.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
You are most welcome, Maestro. I only wish I could have been of more direct assistance during the Master's absence. My apologies again for the inconvenience.

I do hope you find the swift and suitable resolution you seek. Good day to you, Maestro Salieri.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Good day, Signor Benda. I appreciate your understanding and cooperation throughout this process. We shall proceed with caution and ensure the piano is in optimal condition for our upcoming performances. Thank you once again. Farewell.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Farewell, Maestro Salieri. May your concerts be resounding successes.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, Signorina. I look forward to sharing the melodies of my compositions with the world. Farewell, Signorina. Good day.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Ah, Maestro, a moment—it is *Signor* Benda, if you please. But no matter. Good day to you as well, and I truly do wish you the very best with your performances.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Ah, Signora, my apologies for any misunderstanding. Please accept my salutations. Good day to you as well. May your musical endeavors flourish."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Maestro, my apologies, but you persist. It is *Signor* Benda. A journeyman of this workshop, not a Signora. Though I appreciate your kind wishes for my musical endeavours, which, alas, are more often with the hammer and chisel than with the harpsichord.

Good day, Maestro.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Ah, Signor Benda, I understand your position. A journeyman indeed, but still, my regards for your musical pursuits. Good day to you.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Thank you, Maestro Salieri. Yes, a journeyman of the craft, striving to build the instruments that allow *your* musical pursuits to flourish. That is our reward.

Good day, Maestro.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Indeed, Signor Benda, it is a privilege to contribute to the creation of instruments that bring joy and beauty to the world through music. Your efforts in the workshop are invaluable. Good day to you."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
Thank you, Maestro. That is a most generous sentiment, and much appreciated. It truly is an honour to serve the muse in such a way.

Good day to you, Maestro Salieri.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Thank you, Signor Benda. Your words are a testament to the dedication and passion you bring to your craft. Good day to you."
